turns.t: I'm so sorry I'm late, doctor. The parking garage on Fifth was full and I had to circle it twice.
Please don't worry about it, we have plenty of time. Come in and take a seat.
Thank you. I wrote everything down beforehand so I wouldn't forget anything, if that's all right.
More than all right. Notes make my job easier. So what brings you in today?
Mostly a routine check of my nose and throat. It's been about two years since anyone looked.
Think of it as a service for the car. We look under the hood before anything starts rattling. Anything on your list?
Only one item. A coworker told me I should get my airways looked at, and she reads about health constantly.
Fair enough, and I'm glad you came. Let me run through some standard questions. Any nosebleeds?
No nosebleeds. I checked my notes, and not in the last few years either.
Good. What about pain in either ear?
No ear pain at all.
And your breathing in general, any trouble with it, day or night?
It's fine, honestly. I can climb three flights of stairs without stopping.
Great. Now, any health conditions I should know about, things you live with?
Acid reflux, for about six years now. It's mild, and I keep it quiet by eating smaller dinners.
Smaller dinners, sensible. It's like not overfilling a gas tank before a steep hill. Any illnesses that run in the family?
My father has sleep apnea. I put it on the list because I read that it can run in families.
Good thing to flag. And what do you do for work, if you don't mind me asking?
I teach high school chemistry. It's a lot of talking all day, so I'm careful with my voice.
That's like running a marathon in the same pair of shoes every day. Let's get your numbers while you're settled.
Blood pressure is 118 over 76, pulse is 68 and regular, and your temperature is 36.7 degrees Celsius.
Your oxygen saturation is 99 percent, and your respiratory rate is 14 breaths per minute.
Are those good numbers? I printed a table of typical ranges and put it in my folder.
They're textbook. Tidy as a freshly made bed. You can put the folder away.
Wonderful. I'll feel better once I've heard the rest, though. What happens next?
I'll look inside your nose and your throat. Open wide for me and say ahh.
Ahh.
Hm, give me a moment here. The lining inside your nose is a touch swollen on both sides, like a slightly puffy pillow.
Swollen? Should I be worried about that?
Not worried, just interested. Most likely this is mild nasal congestion, the kind of thing that builds up quietly over time.
I see. Is there a way to look further than that? I'd rather know properly.
There is. I'd like to book a nasal endoscopy, a tiny camera on a thin tube that lets us see the whole pipe.
Does that hurt? I'm a little squeamish about anything going up my nose.
It's uncomfortable for a minute, like the tickle before a sneeze, but it's very quick.
Then I can manage that. Will it be done today?
Not today. Our scheduler will call you with a slot, probably within the next couple of weeks.
Perfect. I also have a note about what I could do at home in the meantime.
Run a humidifier at night if you have one, and sip water through your teaching day. Like watering a houseplant.
I have a small humidifier in the bedroom. I'll use it every night, and keep a bottle on my desk.
Then you're ahead of schedule already. I'd like to see you again in four weeks, once the camera test is done.
Four weeks. I'll put it in my calendar right now, hold on.
Take your time. While you type, tell me, are the students behaving this year?
Mostly. The new class is lively, but they love the experiments with the colored flames.
Colored flames, now I wish I'd had you as a teacher. I only remember the baking soda volcano.
Everyone remembers the volcano. We do a bigger version in the spring with a safety shield.
Sounds like a good time. Is there anything else on your list, or have we covered it?
Let me check. Parking, done. Coworker, done. Questions about the test, done. I think that's everything.
Then you did better with that list than most of my appointments do.
Oh, one more thing. Should I bring someone to the camera appointment?
No need, you can drive yourself. It takes ten minutes and you walk out afterwards.
Good, because the garage on Fifth is the only place I know near the clinic.
Try the lot behind the pharmacy. It's usually quiet in the mornings.
The one with the blue gate? I'll try that. Thank you, that's very kind.
My pleasure. Take care of yourself, and enjoy the weekend.
You too, doctor. Goodbye, and thank you again for fitting me in.
Goodbye. Mind the stairs on your way out, they're polished.

chief_complaint.value: a routine check of my nose and throat

physical_examination.finding: lining inside your nose is a touch swollen

clinical_actions.description: Use a humidifier at night and sip water through the day
